newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX rallies onward, sets new records.
newsitem.headline: German DAX rallies onward, sets new records.

text.p: German shares confounded talk of an imminent correction on Tuesday as they took heart from the dollar's gains and good corporate news to set more records, albeit on what traders said were disappointing volumes.
The DAX index advanced 16.50 points, or 0.45 percent to set a new record close of 3,674.36 points, marking an advance of 2.6 percent since Thursday and a 6.9 percent surge in May.
An even stronger earlier rally earlier sent the IBIS DAX of electronic trade as high as 3,691.56 points, but that lost momentum as trading continued, especially since the Bund market was flat.
"We still have our sights on 3,700 (DAX points) and I am confident we will get there," said one trader.
"No matter how people try to talk this market down, we keep setting record after record," another dealer said.
Broad gains were supported by advances of more than three percent on retailer Metro AG and nearly two percent on steelmaker Thyssen AG on the back of strong profit reports.

Metro shares hit an all-time high of 189.90 marks in pre-bourse trade and closed bourse trade up six marks at 184 after it reported its first group profit on ordinary activities of 1.1 billion marks in 1996.
Thyssen hit a high of 404 marks before settling back to trade up 6.60 marks, or 1.7 percent, at 399.10 marks after it reported an 81 percent rise in first half pre-tax profit.
"That was a real surprise and an added boost for the market in the morning," said one trader.
Dealers generally downplayed the fact that the DAX lost so much of its intraday gains.
"We need calm after the past two days," a dealer said of the slowdown. "This is a healthy sign in a market."
